Pgp has a large, flexible drug-binding pocket within the transmembrane domain that can accommodate structurally diverse substrates and inhibitors. Features associated with non-inhibitors: low lipophilicity (logP < 2) — highly polar, hydrophilic molecules do not partition into the membrane to reach the binding site. The test is run both with and without metabolic activation (rat liver S9 fraction) to detect pro-mutagens that require CYP-mediated bioactivation.

Mutagenicity in the Ames test arises through several distinct mechanisms. Direct-acting mutagens are electrophilic species that react covalently with DNA bases — alkylating agents (epoxides, aziridines, nitrogen mustards, alkyl halides), Michael acceptors (α,β-unsaturated carbonyls, acrylates, vinyl sulfones), and acylating agents.
